title: Data Quality Is the Compute Multiplier — Ari Morcos, DatologyAI
talk_summary: Ari Morcos argues that curating training data (cleaning, dedup, quality classifiers, rephrasing into many formats, mixing/sequencing) is a compute multiplier that bends scaling curves, citing 14-point VLM gains and matching Qwen 3.5 with ~145x less training compute.

takeaways.technique: Deduplicate and filter context before it reaches the model
takeaways.what_they_do: They remove semantically redundant documents and low-quality items so each token shown to the model carries maximum marginal information, rather than padding volume.
takeaways.evidence_quote: removing data points that are not the same that are semantically similar but convey very similar information
takeaways.numbers: ~14 absolute percentage point VLM improvement from curation alone

takeaways.technique: Rephrase high-value source material into many task formats
takeaways.what_they_do: They take the highest-quality documents and transform each into hundreds of templates (e.g. true/false questions), increasing diversity and learnability without model collapse because content stays grounded in the source.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we might convert that into one of hundreds of templates. One of which might be a series of true false questions

takeaways.technique: Decontaminate evaluation sets against training/context data
takeaways.what_they_do: They rigorously decontaminate training data against downstream benchmarks with a low n-gram threshold so benchmark scores reflect real capability, not leakage.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we rigorously decontaminate all of our training data with respect to all downstream benchmarks

takeaways.technique: Match data/task distribution to the target task
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue no single dataset is optimal for everything; you must match the data distribution to the specific output tasks you want.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's no one golden data set to rule them all that's good for everything
